title: Pennsylvania's 3rd Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: Pennsylvania's 3rd Congressional District, covering a large portion of Philadelphia, is an open seat following the retirement of longtime incumbent U.S. Rep. Dwight Evans (D), who served from 2016 to 2027. On May 19, 2026, state Rep. Chris Rabb won a competitive four-way Democratic primary with about 45% of the vote, defeating state Sen. Sharif Street, Dr. Ala Stanford, and attorney Shaun Griffith. Rabb, a self-described democratic socialist backed by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and the Working Families Party, ran on a progressive platform of racial and economic justice, universal healthcare, and an end to U.S. aid to Israel. The district is one of the most heavily Democratic in the nation, and with no Republican candidate on the general election ballot, Rabb is expected to win the seat in November.
polling_note: No general election polling was found, as the race is effectively uncontested with only a Democratic candidate on the ballot.

candidates.name: Chris Rabb
candidates.summary: Chris Rabb is a five-term Pennsylvania state representative and the Democratic nominee for Pennsylvania's 3rd Congressional District. A progressive activist and author, he won a four-way primary on May 19, 2026, with the backing of Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, the Working Families Party, and the Democratic Socialists of America. He is unopposed in the general election and expected to succeed retiring U.S. Rep. Dwight Evans.

summary_sources.title: Progressive Rabb wins 3rd District race with boosts from ‘the squad’ and local grassroots activism

career_history.title: State Representative
career_history.description: Five-term representative for Northwest Philadelphia; serves on Agriculture & Rural Affairs, Commerce, Finance, and Judiciary committees.

career_history.title: Author

career_history.description: Taught social entrepreneurship and organizational innovation; helped unionize adjunct professors.

forecast.rationale: Chris Rabb is the only candidate on the general election ballot with no Republican opponent in Pennsylvania's 3rd Congressional District, which is one of the most heavily Democratic districts in the nation. The race is effectively uncontested following the open-seat Democratic primary. No general election polling exists because there is no competitive contest. A Democratic win is a certainty.
